title: The client learns of a release and its staged binary follows (piece 2 of 2026-11
input: The client learns of a release and its staged binary follows (piece 2 of 2026-11-11-004, goal 3 of its concept brief; decisions D-5, D-6, D-7). (1) A daily check from the session-start hook, in a detached process under a lease and a backoff, through one function latestVersion() that fails closed to unknown. (2) The staged binary under <data dir>/bin replaces itself with a verified download, only when no wizardingcode-mem process of an older version holds the store; macOS and Linux; Windows gets the notice only. (3) status, doctor and the viewer's About show the released version and the one command per channel; WIZARDINGCODE_MEM_UPDATE=off|check. (4) One rule for reading the version a staged binary answers, across its five readers (moved here from 2026-11-12-005). (5) The README's privacy section names the daily request and its hosts.

criteria.text: latestRelease sends one GET with redirect: "manual", no body and no header of its own but User-Agent: wizardingcode-mem; it answers the version for a 301 or a 302 whose whole Location is https://github.com/<repository>/releases/tag/v<a>.<b>.<c>, and one of the fixed reasons for anything else (a 200, a 404, a 429, another host, http://, a trailing path, v1.2, a pre-release tag, a number of six digits, a request that throws); it never reads a body; REQUEST_LIMIT_MS is 5000 and a request that never settles answers timed out at the limit given.
distill runs the check after the drain, also when the store cannot be opened, and a check that throws does not change its exit code.

a reconciled command run from a copy older than the staged binary prints the line of J-6 and runs the staged binary with the same arguments, with WIZARDINGCODE_MEM_HANDED=1, returning its exit code; a copy started with that variable set does not hand over; install hands over through the same function.
the test preload turns the check off for every test and every CLI a test starts unless the test sets the key, and distill's and update's tests give them a fake fetch in the test's own process.

the README no longer says "nothing leaves your machine" or "nothing ever leaves your machine", says the daily request in its network bullet with the key that turns it off, names the exception to "every setting can be changed from the viewer", has WIZARDINGCODE_MEM_UPDATE in its settings table and every command of CHANNEL_COMMANDS; the release runbook says that clients are told from the GitHub release and how a notice is withdrawn (gh release edit); ADR 0030 exists and names the redirect, update.json, the two rules for a channel copy and that latest must never start a download; CLAUDE.md names src/update/.

reconciles is true only for status, doctor, update and ui without --auto, over every command of the CLI; decide answers skip on Windows, for a process that is not compiled, whose real path is the staged binary's, with WIZARDINGCODE_MEM_HANDED set, running as root, or with <data dir>/bin not the effective user's, and compare otherwise. --version, --help, no command and an unknown command never reach it.

no file of src/update/ imports from src/store/, src/modules/, src/engine/, src/sync/, src/status/ or src/doctor/; src/cli/main.ts has no static import of src/update/ or src/install/binary.ts; src/cli/reconciled.ts imports nothing.

the automatic check asks only when due: with no state; with any time in the future; one hour after a failure; 24 hours after a success; and not within 60 seconds of an attempt. A forced check asks whatever the state's age. The result is written to <data dir>/update.json: a success records the latest, even a lower one, and clears the reason; a failure keeps the last known version and records the reason. A state file whose latest or reason holds any other text, an escape sequence or a line break included, reads as no state.

the automatic check makes no request when WIZARDINGCODE_MEM_UPDATE is off or any value but check, from the environment or from <data dir>/env, or when CI is set; a forced check makes no request when the key is off or any value but check, and makes one when only CI is set; the settings refuse any value of the key but check and off.

doctor prints a check update: warn when a release is out, ok otherwise, the failed check included, and its exit code is what it is without that check; the checks runChecks returns do not include it. wizardingcode-mem update asks now, prints the lines and the four commands, and exits 1 when its check failed or its result could not be recorded; with the key off it asks nothing, prints the off line and how to turn the check on where the value was set (the file, or this environment), prints no commands, and exits 0.

updateLine gives line 1 by the Design's first table, top to bottom: off from the file; off from the environment; an unknown value; a latest known and higher than the current, with and without a failed last check, and with the staged binary answering a version and not; CI with nothing asked; never checked; a failed check with and without a last known version; the latest equal; the latest lower. Line 2 follows the second table: none for the staged binary itself, for no staged file and for equal versions; the plain sentence for a higher staged version; wizardingcode-mem install moves them to it for a lower one; wizardingcode-mem install replaces it for a staged file that answers no version. status prints them with the commands when a release is out; with a store that cannot be opened it still prints them and exits 1, and status --json then prints one object with version, update and error. No command but install stages a binary.

status, doctor and update do not run the staged file when the command runs as root or when <data dir>/bin belongs to another user: the report says the staged binary was not run and why, and takes the running copy as the current version. A report that cannot be built is said with its reason in status, as in doctor, and a reconciliation that throws lets the command run in this copy.

decisions.question: The scope after six lenses found four blockers in the self-replacement (D-6 of 2026-11-11-004): tell and add two pieces with no network, replace only where no channel manager exists, or keep the self-replacement on every channel?
decisions.default: Tell, plus the two pieces with no network; the self-replacement becomes a later item of its own
decisions.answer: Avisar + sem rede: this item tells (status, doctor, About) and adds the two pieces with no network (a newer Homebrew or npm copy stages itself when run; any command of an older copy hands over to the newer staged binary); the automatic replacement becomes an item of its own, after signatures or a hold signal exist. The author's choice in the question dialog on 2026-11-12.

decisions.question: The default of WIZARDINGCODE_MEM_UPDATE for the daily request to github.com: on (notice only) or off?
decisions.default: On, notice only; off with the key; never in CI
decisions.answer: Ligada, só aviso: it checks once a day and shows the released version, never replaces anything; the README names the request among its exceptions; off with the key, and off in CI. The author's choice in the question dialog on 2026-11-12.

decisions.question: A newer channel copy run with status or doctor: does it stage itself (the hooks then run it at once, in the open session, while that session's MCP server, sync and viewer stay on the old one), or does it only tell?
decisions.default: It only tells, and names wizardingcode-mem install as the command that moves the agents
decisions.answer: Só avisa: status and doctor from a newer copy say which version the agents run and that wizardingcode-mem install moves them; nothing changes without an explicit command, as today. The author's choice in the question dialog on 2026-11-12, after the review's design reader showed the staging would take effect in the open session.

It never follows the redirect and never reads a body.
